issues.body:
mask_quotes_and_expressions() blanks the CONTENTS of double-quoted strings before SWALLOW_RE is applied. A command substitution written as `"$( ... )"` is inside double quotes, so any swallow within it is erased before matching.

Reproduced on the PR head:

  in : num="$(python3 scripts/resolve-merge-group-pr.py x || true)"
  out: 'num="                                                      "'   -> find_swallows() = 0 hits
  in : num=$(python3 scripts/resolve-merge-group-pr.py x || true)      -> 1 hit

End-to-end: a synthetic gating job whose run body is `out="$(python3 scripts/coverage-gate.py --check || true)"` makes the checker print "check-workflow-run-swallow: all clear (W1 + W2 + W3 + W4)".

This is not hypothetical. Comparing a raw scan of gating job blocks against scan(), 29 gating-job `|| true` lines exist on main but only 22 are detected. The 7 missed, all of this shape:
  bead-autoclose.yml:close-merged-beads      SUBJECT="$(git log -1 --format=%s "$MERGE_SHA" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  ci.yml:coverage-demoted-filer              | head -n1 || true)"
  ci.yml:heavy-recall-demoted-filer          | head -n1 || true)"
  flow-on-gates.yml:quick-gates              --jq '.[0].number' 2>/dev/null || true)"
  flow-on-gates.yml:quick-gates              num="$(python3 scripts/resolve-merge-group-pr.py "${MERGE_HEAD_REF:-}" || true)"
  slsa-builder-pin-review.yml:review         count="$(printf '%s' "$refs" | grep -c . || true)"
  vectors-aarch64.yml:neon                   listed="$(grep -c 'simd::tests::' "${out}" || true)"

So the frozen inventory is 24% short, and every one of those 7 is a pre-authorised shape a future edit can hide behind. The file's own header states the threat as "an assertion could be neutralised in a gating lane with a two-character edit and no reviewer signal" — after this PR, wrapping the assignment in quotes is that two-character edit.
issues.fix_hint: Make the masker command-substitution aware: when scanning a double-quoted region, do not blank the interior of a `$( ... )` (track paren depth and recurse, or pre-extract `$( ... )` spans and scan them as their own logical statements before masking). Keep the masking length-preserving so the real/masked index alignment head_command() depends on is not broken. Then add self-test fixtures for `out="$(cmd || true)"`, `: "$(cmd || true)"`, and the multi-line `"$(cmd \ | head -n1 || true)"` form, and add the 7 now-visible sites to .github/run-swallow-waivers.json with reasons (several are genuine `grep -c` no-match data outcomes and will waive cleanly). If closing this is deliberately deferred, the header must state the bound explicitly the way W2 does, and the 22-vs-29 numbers must say why they differ.
issues.title: W1 is blind to `|| true` inside a double-quoted command substitution — 7 of the repo's 29 real gating swallow sites are undetected, evadable with two quote characters

issues.body:
find_continue_on_error() locates steps with STEP_START_RE = `^(\s*)-\s+(?:name:\s*(.*)|(?:uses|run):\s*)`. A step whose first mapping key is anything else never sets step_indent, and YAML places no constraint on key order.

Three fixtures, each a gating job with a step-level `continue-on-error: true`, all reported "all clear":

  g1:  - continue-on-error: true      # CONTINUE_ON_ERROR_RE is anchored ^(\s*)continue-on-error:, the `- ` prefix defeats it
         name: assertion
         run: cargo test

  g2:  - id: step-with-id-first        # STEP_START_RE does not match, step_indent stays None -> hit skipped
         run: cargo test
         continue-on-error: true

  g3:  - if: always()                  # same
         run: cargo test
         continue-on-error: true

`- if:` and `- id:` are ordinary spellings and already appear in this repo (nightly-full-sweep.yml:97, ci.yml:3890). A secondary effect: when a step begins with an unmatched key mid-job, step_indent/step_name retain the PREVIOUS step's values, so a hit that is detected can be attributed to the wrong step name — and since the W4 waiver `match` text is built from that name (`f"{step_name}: continue-on-error: ..."`), a waiver can bind to the wrong step.
issues.fix_hint: Detect a step boundary from the list-item dash alone rather than from a key allowlist: match `^(\s*)-\s+\S` to set step_indent, then capture `name:` opportunistically (from the dash line or any later line at step_indent+2) for the label. Also let CONTINUE_ON_ERROR_RE match the dash form, e.g. `^(\s*)(?:-\s+)?continue-on-error:\s*(.*?)\s*(?:#.*)?$`, treating the dash line's own indent as the step indent. Add the three fixtures above to _w4_cases().
issues.title: W4 misses step-level `continue-on-error` whenever the step's first key is not name/uses/run (`- if:`, `- id:`, or `- continue-on-error:` itself)

issues.body:
The header says: "Inventory taken 2026-09-02 ... 57 of them inside jobs that GATE (29 `|| true`, 7 `set +e`, 21 bare `exit 0`)" and then "Under this checker's own (narrower, see below) scope those 57 resolve to 22 `|| true` sites in gating jobs, every one of them declared in the waiver file".

The only narrowing the "see below" text actually explains is the deliberate exclusion of bare `exit 0` (21 sites, with a correct errexit argument). Nothing explains why 29 `|| true` becomes 22. The answer is the blind spot in the first issue — those 7 are not out of scope by decision, the parser cannot see them. As written the reader concludes the clean inventory is complete and frozen when 24% of it is unrepresented, and W1's own text ("There is NO exemption by command name ... every site — diagnostic ones included — is declared ONCE") reinforces a completeness claim the code does not meet.

This matters because the surrounding discipline is otherwise scrupulous: W2 states its bound ("a SECOND command placed after a valid capture in the same region is not covered"), and the pages.yml waiver carries an explicit "STATED BOUND". The same standard should apply here. The `_doc` string in .github/run-swallow-waivers.json inherits the claim ("W1 covers statement-level `|| true` / `|| :`") without qualification.
issues.fix_hint: Either close the gap (preferred — see the first issue) so 29 == 29, or keep the current scope and say so plainly: state that `|| true` inside a double-quoted command substitution is not currently detected, name the 7 known sites, and file the follow-up bead. Reconcile the `_doc` string in .github/run-swallow-waivers.json to the same bound.
issues.title: Header overstates W1 coverage: the 29 -> 22 drop is presented as "narrower scope" when it is an undisclosed parser blind spot

issues.body:
extract_run_blocks() passes every line through _ADV._strip_shell_comments(), which does `re.split(r"\s#", line, maxsplit=1)[0]`. That is deliberately crude for the advisory registry's purposes, but here it removes text this checker must see.

Reproduced: a gating job with
  python3 scripts/coverage-gate.py --check --title "a # b" || true
is NOT flagged, because the line is truncated at ` # ` and the `|| true` never reaches SWALLOW_RE. (The adjacent `grep -q "## Required section" CHANGELOG.md || true` IS flagged, since `"##` has no preceding whitespace — so the behaviour is inconsistent as well as lossy.)

Lower severity than the command-substitution gap because it needs a whitespace-padded `#` inside a quoted argument, but this repo's workflows do pass markdown bodies to `gh issue comment` and similar, so it is reachable.
issues.fix_hint: Do comment stripping AFTER quote masking rather than before: mask the line first, find the first `#` that is preceded by whitespace AND lies outside a masked quoted span, and truncate the real line at that index. Add a fixture asserting `cmd --title "a # b" || true` is still flagged.
issues.title: Comment stripping is not quote-aware, so `|| true` after a `#` inside a quoted argument is dropped

issues.body:
The 39 cases are genuine and non-vacuous — the W1 parse cases pin the resolved head verb, the W2 cases distinguish captured/branched/printed/unused status, and the advisory-job cases confirm gating scope is respected. I ran them: 39/39 PASS.

The gap is dimensional. Every W1 fixture uses an unquoted statement-level swallow, and every W4 fixture uses a step whose first key is `name:`. So the suite is green while both false-negative classes are live, which is precisely the situation the suite exists to prevent — a passing self-test is currently evidence about the parser's known-good paths only, not about its coverage.
issues.fix_hint: Add negative fixtures alongside the fixes: W1 for `out="$(cmd || true)"`, `: "$(cmd || true)"` and the multi-line `| head -n1 || true)"` continuation; W4 for the `- if:`-first, `- id:`-first and `- continue-on-error:`-first step shapes. Each should be a `want 1` case that fails against today's code.
issues.title: Self-test is thorough on the parsing bugs it already fixed but has no fixture for either confirmed blind spot

issues.body:
waiver_matches() tests `str(waiver["match"]) in site["command"]` and check() does `used.update(matched)`, so a single waiver can mark any number of sites as declared. If a job later grows a second swallow whose command text contains an existing waiver's match string, it is waived with no new declaration and no W3 signal.

The 12-char MIN_MATCH_LENGTH and the workflow+job_id scoping keep today's 25 entries narrow enough that I found no live over-match (25 sites / 25 waivers, one-to-one). Raising it now is not required — noting it because the file describes itself as "a ratchet, not an approval list", and an N:1 waiver-to-site binding is the one way the ratchet can loosen without an edit to this file.
issues.fix_hint: Optional hardening: assert one waiver binds to at most one site (report a W3-style offence when len(matched sites) > 1 for a single waiver), so a newly-grown swallow that collides with an existing match must be declared explicitly.
issues.title: Substring `match` lets one waiver silently cover additional future sites in the same job

verdict.summary:
A well-motivated CI ratchet (W1-W4) that freezes the existing inventory of failure-swallowing idioms in gating GitHub Actions jobs. The design is sound in outline: it reuses check-advisory-registry.py's parse_jobs/load_registry so "which jobs gate" cannot drift, it correctly refuses a name-based exemption list, the waiver schema is enforced (required fields + a 12-char minimum match + W3 staleness), and the wiring lands in docs-quality.yml's `quick-gates` job, which I confirmed is NOT in advisory-registry.json (i.e. it really gates) with both the self-test and enforce steps unswallowed. --self-test passes 39/39 and the live run is clean at 25 sites / 25 waivers.

But the checker has two confirmed false-negative classes, both verified empirically against the PR head:

1. BLOCKER: W1 cannot see `|| true` inside a DOUBLE-QUOTED command substitution. mask_quotes_and_expressions() blanks double-quoted contents before SWALLOW_RE runs, so `out="$(gate.sh || true)"` is invisible while the unquoted `out=$(gate.sh || true)` is caught. I reproduced this: a synthetic gating job containing `out="$(python3 scripts/coverage-gate.py --check || true)"` reports "all clear". On the repo's own workflows this misses 7 of the 29 real gating-job `|| true` sites (24%), including slsa-builder-pin-review.yml:review, flow-on-gates.yml:quick-gates and vectors-aarch64.yml:neon. Adding two quote characters is exactly the "two-character edit" neutralisation the file's own header says it closes.

2. MAJOR: W4 misses step-level `continue-on-error` whenever the step's first key is not name/uses/run. `- if:`, `- id:` and `- continue-on-error:` first all went undetected in a 3-job fixture.

Also an honesty gap: the header reports the 29 -> 22 reduction as "narrower scope" without disclosing (1), while W2 and the pages.yml waiver both state their bounds explicitly.

The checker is worth landing once these blind spots are closed or honestly stated; as written it advertises coverage it does not have.
